1.

Petitioner has filed this writ petition aggrieved with the action of sealing of her shops No. G-1, 2,
3, 4 & 5 at Cross Road Business Park, Vyapar Vihar, Bilaspur by respondent No.5 without issuing any notice or passing any order against petitioner.

2. Learned counsel for petitioner submits that petitioner has established two units namely Daily Dose Bakery and Xero Degree Cafe in shop No. G-1, 2, 3, 4 & 5 of ground floor of Cross Road Business Park situated in front of Mahima Complex, Vyapar Vihar Bilaspur after obtaining valid Gumasta license, food license etc.
The said shops are owned by respondent No.6, who executed the lease deed in favour of proprietor of petitioner's firm on 31st of October, 2022.

At the time of execution of lease deed, respondent No.6 informed petitioner that shopping complex was constructed after fulfilling all the formalities, obtaining due permission from the competent authority in accordance with law.
After taking aforementioned shops on lease, petitioner invested huge amount for starting aforementioned business.
Respondent No.5 on 28.02.2023 suddenly came to the shop of petitioner and sealed the shop let out to petitioner on which petitioner is running her business.

3. It is further contention of learned counsel for petitioner that before taking adverse action of sealing the entire running shops of petitioner no notice of any kind has been served upon petitioner and even she was not informed about the same by respondent No.5 as to for what reasons, the shops have been sealed.

He contended that petitioner thereafter also approached the authorities i.e. the office of respondents No.2 and 5 to know about the reason and the provision under which her shops were sealed, however, they have not given any information nor served with any order till the date of filing of writ petition.
The action on the part of respondent no.2 and 5 is highly arbitrary and in violation of Article 19 (1) (g) of the Constitution of India.

Referring to the reply submitted by respondents No.2 and 5 he contended that in reply, there is pleading that shops occupied by petitioner was sealed for the purpose of demolition of fourth floor which was illegally constructed which also is after thought.

According to her information, even the respondent No.6 was not served with any notice, even if any part of building is unauthorizedly constructed without prior approval and permission of the competent authority.
Hence, entire action of on the part of respondents is not sustainable.
Therefore, respondents be directed to unseal the shops of petitioner immediately.

4. Learned counsel for respondents No.6 submits that respondent No.2 and 5 have not issued any notice to respondent No.6 at any point of time before taking action of sealing of shops leased out to petitioner.

It is contention of learned counsel for respondent No.6 that respondent No.6 has already submitted an application for regularization of construction along with map which is pending consideration and which is also acknowledged by respondents No.2 and 5 in their return.

5. Learned counsel for respondents No.2 and 5 submits that there is no dispute with respect to running of business by petitioner on the shop No. G-1, 2, 3, 4 & 5 at Cross Road Business Park,
Vyapar Vihar, Bilaspur after obtaining those shops on lease from respondent No.6.
There is no direct conflicting issue with petitioner but with respondent no.6 on account of illegal construction of fourth floor.
Respondent No.6 had applied for building permission, which was allowed and he was permitted to construct complex in terms of the proposal submitted and accepted by answering respondents.

Respondent No.6 completed the construction of 3rd floor of the aforementioned A And B Foods vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 4 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/46616612/
2 complex along with basement according to proposal.

sentences.text: He has also been issued completion certificate for the same.
Respondent No.6 by deceiving the answering respondents obtained completion certificate, however, he continued with the construction of one more floor i.e. fourth floor.
After getting knowledge of illegal construction of fourth floor by respondent No.6, notice was issued to him, however, he did not appear nor replied the said notice.

Some complaints were also received against petitioner, hence, respondent No.4 also joined with respondent No.5 along with State machinery and visited the complex of respondent No.6 on 28.02.2023 to take actions against illegal construction and the violation of food norms by petitioner.
Respondent No.4 proceeded to move against petitioner and the rest of the team proceeded to move against other operational shops.
He also argued that respondent No.4 took few samples and thereafter answering respondents moved ahead with their procedure.
It is further contention of learned counsel for respondent No.2 & 5 that samples collected by respondent No.4 was found to be sub-standard.
Petitioner is trying to bypass and move around the notice of eviction served upon respondent No.6 for which petitioner is having the alternate remedy.

The claim of petitioner that no action has been taken against respondent No.6 but only against petitioner is not correct as the action is being taken only against respondent No.6 and not against any other persons.
6. In reply, learned counsel for petitioner submits that it is the complex of three floor in which more than 40 shops are constructed out of which shops of petitioner is only sealed.
7. I have heard learned counsel for parties and perused the documents placed on record.
8. The main contention of learned counsel for petitioner is that shop of petitioner is sealed without any authority of law and that too by adopting pick and choose method only.
From the pleadings made in the reply it is reflecting that respondents have clearly pleaded that no direct conflicting issue is there against petitioner.
Sealing of shops of petitioner was done by respondents No.2 and 5 and further no notice to petitioner, if any, issued, is placed on record.

9. From the aforementioned facts it is appearing that there is no dispute on the submission of learned counsel for petitioner that action taken against petitioner who is in possession of particular shops and running the business has been taken without issuing any show cause notice to her and giving any opportunity of hearing.

From the reply it is also reflecting that respondent No.2 and 5 sealed the shops on the ground that shops which petitioner is occupied are in building of respondent No.6 who is raising construction of unauthorized fourth floor.
Shop of petitioner was sealed for the purpose of demolition of fourth floor.

It is not the case of respondents No.2 and 5 that entire building of respondent No.6 is unauthorizedly constructed without prior approval from the competent authority nor it is a case of respondent no.2 and 5 that shop which is possessed by petitioner after taking on lease is illegally constructed but the reply of respondent No.2 and 5 is that fourth floor which respondent No.6 is constructing is unauthorized and illegal as pleaded in reply also.
The action which can be taken under the Act of 1956 is only on the part of the building said to be constructed without prior permission of the authority.

10. In the aforementioned facts of the case, where the submission of learned counsel for petitioner that out of more than 40 shops, only shops of petitioner are sealed is also not disputed in specific A And B Foods vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 4 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/46616612/
3 terms.

sentences.text:
Respondent No.6 has already submitted an application for regularization of construction of fourth floor which is pending consideration before respondent No.2 and 5.
11.
Section 308-A of the Municipal Corporation Act, 1956 deals with compounding of offence of construction of buildings without permission.
The Commissioner i.e. respondent No.2 is still to apply his mind and decide the application for regularization of construction in terms of Section 308-A of the Municipal Corporation Act, 1956.

12. In the aforementioned facts and circumstances of the case, where the action of sealing of the shops occupied by petitioner and running business in those shops is without issuing any show cause notice in the opinion of this Court is arbitrary exercise of power, hence it is not sustainable in the eyes of law.
13. For the forgoing discussions made hereinabove, this petition is allowed.
Respondent No.2 and 5 are directed to unseal the shops, subject matter of writ petition forthwith without any further delay.
No order as to costs.
